title: Condensed-point pullback preserves unbounded derived internal Hom
statement:
Let $X$ be any scheme with its small pro-etale site and compatible coefficient universes [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\Lambda$ be any commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. Let $p_X$ be the condensed-point morphism with exact symmetric monoidal inverse image [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback], and put $B=p_X^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use internal module categories [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], their ordinary uncompleted unbounded derived categories [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], derived relative tensor and internal Hom [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom], and the K-injective ringed-site description [def-pur-derived-internal-hom, def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. For arbitrary $K,L\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda})$, the evaluation-adjoint comparison
$$\beta_{X,K,L}:p_X^*R\mathcal Hom_{\Lambda}(K,L)\longrightarrow R\mathcal Hom_B(p_X^*K,p_X^*L)$$
is an isomorphism. The morphism is specified before asserting invertibility: its tensor-Hom transpose is
$$p_X^*R\mathcal Hom_{\Lambda}(K,L)\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}p_X^*K\cong p_X^*(R\mathcal Hom_{\Lambda}(K,L)\otimes_{\Lambda}^{\mathbf L}K)\xrightarrow{p_X^*\mathrm{ev}}p_X^*L.$$
It is natural contravariantly in $K$ and covariantly in $L$. For every pro-etale test $W\to X$, restriction to the localized ringed site [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], with the canonical derived tensor, Hom and coefficient comparisons, identifies $\beta_{X,K,L}|_W$ with $\beta_{W,K,L}$ as a derived morphism. No boundedness, finite generation, dualizability, discrete coefficient or completeness assumption is imposed on $K,L,\Lambda$.

source.place: Proposition 4.3(1) and (4.1): agent globalization along the geometrically w-contractible affine basis, with slice restriction of derived internal Hom.

proof.text: Use the internal-module/section-ring equivalence, which leaves underlying sheaves and morphisms unchanged. On the scheme and its slices, the module-object derived comparison identifies the native relative derived tensor and internal Hom with the ringed-site ones and carries evaluation to evaluation. On the condensed point, use the same section-ring presentation on the site of profinite sets: the internal-section tensor comparison, valid on any site whose abelian sheafification has monoidal local equivalences, identifies the relative tensor of internal $\Lambda$-modules with the ringed-site tensor over the section-ring sheaf and preserves and reflects K-flat complexes, so the native derived relative tensor over $\Lambda$ is the ringed-site K-flat derived tensor; the derived-internal-Hom sections model identifies the right adjoint defining internal Hom with the K-injective model. Thus it suffices to prove the assertion in these ringed-site presentations, with their specified evaluation maps; all coefficient rings remain the original pulled-back condensed rings.

source.place: Tag 08J7, section-internal-hom; K-injective model and uniqueness of the tensor right adjoint; Hemo–Richarz–Scholbach Section 3, ordinary unbounded coefficient categories

proof.text: Put $H=R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(K,L)$. The derived tensor pullback theorem gives $p_X^*H\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}p_X^*K\cong p_X^*(H\otimes_\Lambda^{\mathbf L}K)$. Compose this with $p_X^*\mathrm{ev}$ and take its transpose under the derived tensor-Hom adjunction. This defines exactly $\beta_{X,K,L}$ in the statement. Naturality of evaluation and of that adjunction shows that the transposes commute with precomposition in $K$ and postcomposition in $L$, proving both requested naturalities before invertibility is used. Exactness of the inverse image means its derived functor is its termwise functor, so there is no boundedness restriction in this construction.

source.place: Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product; Tag 08J9, lemma-internal-hom and equation-internal-hom

proof.text: Let $j:W\to X$ be any object of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, and write $r$ for restriction to $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/W$. The site-equivalence clause of weakly-etale localization identifies this slice with $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Under this identification the abelian inverse image along $j$ is restriction to the localized site, and the coefficient isomorphism $j^*B\cong p_W^*\Lambda$ is the canonical one, by the coefficient-sections localization lemma. Hence the condensed-point composition comparison identifies $r p_X^*$ with $p_W^*$, including on coefficient rings, modules and their termwise derived categories. Restriction of derived internal Hom identifies the target of $r\beta_X$ with $R\mathcal Hom_{p_W^*\Lambda}(p_W^*K,p_W^*L)$. More precisely, the slice evaluation-transpose theorem says that the transpose of this transported $r\beta_X$ is $r$ of the defining map in step 2, followed by the inverse tensor restriction comparison. Its evaluation equation identifies this map with $p_W^*\mathrm{ev}$ after the tensor comparison. The composition comparisons are monoidal, so these are the same tensor comparison and coefficient identification as for $p_W^*$. Uniqueness under the adjunction therefore gives $r\beta_{X,K,L}=\beta_{W,K,L}$ as derived morphisms. This proves the entire restriction clause, for arbitrary tests, independently of the local calculation below.

source.place: Tags 08JB (lemma-restriction-RHom-to-U), 08FI (lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open) and 07A4; site localization uses 094T and 0951 as recorded in the cited localization node

proof.text: Now let $W$ be a w-contractible affine test, put $S=\pi_0(W)$ and use $p_W=q_S\pi_W$. The functor $q_S^*$ is precisely restriction from the profinite site to its localized site $\operatorname{Prof}/S$, with ring $\Lambda_S=q_S^*\Lambda$. Consequently the ringed-site restriction theorem gives an isomorphism $a:q_S^*R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(K,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_{\Lambda_S}(q_S^*K,q_S^*L)$. The slice evaluation-transpose theorem says specifically that $a$ is the comparison whose transpose is $q_S^*\mathrm{ev}$ with the tensor restriction comparison; it is not an arbitrarily chosen isomorphism of objects.

source.place: Equation (4.1) and the paragraph preceding Proposition 4.3; profinite slice restriction is Stacks 08JB with the evaluation normalization of 08J9

proof.text: Apply the w-contractible component derived-Hom theorem to $q_S^*K,q_S^*L$. Its evaluation-adjoint comparison $b:\pi_W^*R\mathcal Hom_{\Lambda_S}(q_S^*K,q_S^*L)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_{p_W^*\Lambda}(\pi_W^*q_S^*K,\pi_W^*q_S^*L)$ is invertible. Under $p_W^*\cong\pi_W^*q_S^*$, the composite $b\circ\pi_W^*a$ is $\beta_W$: its tensor-Hom transpose is first $\pi_W^*$ of the transpose of $a$, then evaluation after pullback, hence is $(\pi_W^*q_S^*)\mathrm{ev}$ with the composite tensor comparison. This is the defining transpose of $\beta_W$ from step 2. Therefore $\beta_W$ is a composite of two isomorphisms. The component theorem applies to arbitrary unbounded objects over an arbitrary condensed ring; in particular no perfectness or discrete-coefficient hypothesis was needed.

source.place: Proposition 4.3(1), preservation of inner homomorphisms, combined with factorization (4.1); the composite comparison is identified by the tensor-Hom counit formula

proof.text: Take a cone $C$ of $\beta_X$. Restriction is induced termwise by an exact module functor, so it commutes with cohomology and carries this cone triangle to the cone triangle of the restricted map. By steps 3 and 5, $C|_W=0$ for every w-contractible affine test $W$. Hence $H^n(C)|_W=0$ for every integer $n$ and every such $W$. Every object of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ has a covering by these affines; a section of $H^n(C)$ restricts to zero on that covering and is therefore zero by separatedness of a sheaf. Thus every $H^n(C)$ is zero, so $C=0$ in the ordinary unbounded derived category and $\beta_X$ is invertible. No passage through a completed or bounded subcategory has occurred. For the empty scheme the same assertion holds in the zero module category; zero objects and shifts of arbitrary unbounded objects require no modification.
